lines.text: Medicare Part B will cost two hundred nine dollars and forty cents a month in twenty twenty-seven.
That's up six dollars and fifty cents, or three point two percent.
And the yearly deductible rises to two hundred ninety-two dollars.
The good news? Social Security's twenty twenty-seven raise is three point six percent.
For the first time since twenty twenty-three, Medicare is rising slower than your raise.
Last year, the premium jumped seventeen dollars and ninety cents, against a two point eight percent raise.
Say your check is two thousand dollars. The raise adds seventy-two.
Medicare takes back six fifty. You keep about sixty-five fifty.
Follow for more quiet money breakdowns.
